title: Play of the year! The way in which @Playwrights Horizons continuously...
transcript: I got to see degenerates, which is the newest play by theatre power couple Else Went and Emma Rosa Went, the same duo behind last year's Initiative that I absolutely adored, which was the five hour epic about high schoolers playing D&D. One of the aspects that I loved about initiative was how Else Went in her writing, got you to empathize with characters that you normally wouldn't empathize with, and she has taken that skill from Initiative and multiplied it by 1,000 for Degenerates. Degenerates dives into the cesspool of incel culture, taking us into a private discord where incels find solace in this shared ideology that infects so many young men today in America. And else gets you to feel empathy for these characters, even when they struggle to give that to themselves. On the two vastly different journeys that this play takes you on, you find yourself both rooting for these characters and wanting the best for humanity, while simultaneously being horrified at the ease at which these characters discuss these ideas. This is a play that left me feeling gross and uncomfortable. Both uncomfortable with the subject matter at hand, but also uncomfortable with how comfortable I got in hearing these characters talk the way that they did and relating, in a way, to the sorrow that they feel in this play, despite how rancid I think their core ideology is. And on top of this incredible play by Else Went, you have this direction. By Emma Rosa Went. That really helps to bring this to life through the design elements, through the movement in the show. Just the things that the characters will do in their rooms alone as they are finding human connection on the other side of a screen was fascinating to watch. There was a scenic transition in this that made me choke up. It was just so good. I truly think Degenerates is one of my favorite plays of the year. I immediately left that theater and went, oh! Oh, Pulitzer. And after falling in love with initiative last year, anytime that I see both Else and Emma Rosa Went, are involved in any piece of theater, I will be there. That is how good this show is. I cannot recommend it enough. The good news, if the time of Initiative scared you off, this play is considerably shorter, clocking in at just under three hours. But when I tell you this feels like it was five minutes long, I was that engrossed. As far as tickets go, I did get a last minute rush ticket to this. They do offer $35 rush tickets at the box office. I will say I did go the day of the Nor'easter, so may have been a little easier to get tickets that day, but I cannot recommend trying to get them enough. I do believe there's also a digital rush on TodayTix. The main thing is get to this play if you can. They have extended it multiple times because it keeps selling out. The latest extension takes all the way to November 1st. If you can get to Playrights Horizons before November 1st, please, please do. I love Degenerates so much, and it just feels like a play that is so incredibly timely for the world that we're in in more ways than one.
